bullets.text: Underwriting margin reached 7.6% (beating the 4% target); net income hit a record $667.3 million; ROE reached 19.3%; and 48 of 49 personal lines regulatory markets operated profitably.
Companywide NPW grew 30% (+$2.2B); Personal Lines NPW rose 29% to $8.4B; Direct NPW increased 36%, Agent grew 26%, and Commercial Auto surpassed $1B in written premium (+50%+).

Personal lines auto PIF increased 22% (Agent +22%, Direct +27%); Commercial Auto PIF +38%; Special Lines PIF grew nearly 20%; policy life estimates lengthened significantly across distribution channels and lines.

Investment portfolio returned 5.5% (fixed income 10.1%, equities -21.5%); ~$200M OTTI recognized; shareholders' equity ended at $3.77B; $400M debt issued; completed a 3:1 stock split and repurchased 3.6M shares.

Competitors withdrew, constrained new business, filed double-digit rate hikes, or became insolvent from inadequate prior rates, reinsurance limits, and investment losses; top 15 company market share consolidated to about 70%.
Over 90 rate and program revisions executed across 49 regulatory markets to maintain adequacy; 48 of 49 personal lines markets operated profitably, most at or above the 4% target margin.

Results reflected relatively few catastrophes and an unexpected drop in claim frequency; loss adjustment expenses were reduced, file quality improved, and settlements of several class-action lawsuits reflected approximately $85 million in 2002 results.
Earned No. 3 rank in U.S. private passenger auto, climbing 31 places in 20 years; held 5.9% personal auto market share; led motorcycle insurance with an approximate 25% market share.

Expense ratio was comparable to or lower than any agency-distributing competitor; over 60% of agent policy change requests were made directly by agents; hired over 3,000 claim representatives (1 per 60 applicants).

Ended homeowners insurance initiative after concluding it failed to meet auto-support objectives; created the first insurance product for Segway Human Transporters; expanded vehicle claims repair process prototypes to seven sites.
